title: Security review - Encryption, KMS, BYOK/HSM (Nimbus Analytics)
summary: Customer wanted a focused security review on encryption at rest/in transit and key management options. Discussed Redwood-managed keys vs BYOK with cloud KMS and HSM-backed keys, key rotation, envelope encryption, audit logging, and data residency. Agreed next steps: share security pack (SOC2/ISO reports), schedule SE-led technical BYOK trial, and provide pricing/options for HSM-backed contract add-on.
action_items: Alyssa Chen: Share Redwood security pack (SOC 2 Type II, ISO27001 summary, pen test report) by 2025-12-05
Miguel Santos: Schedule BYOK technical deep dive and demo with Nimbus infra team (target week of 2025-12-15)
Jordan Patel: Provide HSM options and pricing add-on (Thales/CloudHSM vs managed KMS) by 2025-12-09
Priya Raman: Provide list of required compliance controls and any regional key residency constraints by 2025-12-08
next_steps: Send security pack and SOC2/ISO artifacts
Run BYOK test using customer's AWS KMS CMKs in sandbox
Confirm SLA and HSM pricing for Dedicated/Private deployment
Schedule follow-up technical call for end-to-end key rotation scenario
transcript:
[00:00] Alyssa Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um today we wanted to walk through encryption and key management options for Redwood and how that maps to Nimbus' requirements.
[00:18] Priya Raman: Thanks, Alyssa. We have some strict requirements around customer-owned keys and regional restrictions, and Liam will cover our security bar.
[00:30] Liam O'Connor: Right, mainly concerned about BYOK, HSM-backed keys, and whether Redwood has FIPS-compliant paths and how audit logs look end to end.
[00:45] Miguel Santos: Cool, I'll start with an overview. Redwood supports encryption in transit by default with TLS 1.2/1.3, certs managed, and at rest we use envelope encryption. For keys we have three primary models: Redwood-managed KMS, cloud-integrated KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure) with customer CMKs (BYOK), and HSM-backed keys for Private/Dedicated.
[01:12] Sara Kim: When you say envelope encryption, is the data key ever stored plain on your side?
[01:20] Miguel Santos: No, data keys are encrypted with a higher-level key. The encrypted data key is stored with the blob, we never store plaintext data keys. There are occasional transcription quirks in docs call it KV cache but it's actually our metadata store.
[01:38] Liam O'Connor: For BYOK, do you support importing a CMK or do we have to create it in our KMS and grant Redwood access?
[01:47] Jordan Patel: Best practice is you create the CMK in your cloud KMS and then grant Redwood service principal access to encrypt/decrypt operations. We also support an HSM-backed flow where the keys never leave the HSM — either cloud HSM like AWS CloudHSM or an on-prem Thales/Entrust device for Private deployments.
[02:10] Priya Raman: And how is key rotation handled? We need to rotate keys quarterly and make sure old data stays decryptable.
[02:18] Miguel Santos: We do key versioning; envelope encryption lets you rewrap data keys with a new master key while keeping ciphertext around. For rotation we support automated rewrap jobs or staged rotations — we can kick off a rewrap in the background. For BYOK, rotation is coordinated with your KMS: you rotate the CMK and we stop using the old one after the grace period you define.
[02:42] Priya Raman: Is there any scenario where Redwood has access to plaintext?
[02:47] Jordan Patel: No. With BYOK + HSM, Redwood only receives encrypted tokens. For Redwood-managed keys, we hold the master key and can decrypt — that's why some customers require BYOK for zero-escrow guarantees.
[03:01] Liam O'Connor: We need attestations — can you provide FIPS/FedRAMP guidance?
[03:06] Alyssa Chen: We can share our compliance pack; Redwood itself is SOC 2 Type II and we have ISO27001 scope for the platform. For HSM specifics, we reference FIPS 140-2/140-3 validated modules when using CloudHSM or third-party HSMs.
[03:24] Sara Kim: Audit logs — do you surface KMS operations to us? We want to see key usage in CloudTrail or equivalent.
[03:31] Miguel Santos: Yes, for cloud-integrated KMS operations you'll see KMS events in your CloudTrail / Audit Logs. Additionally, Redwood emits application-level audit logs (which operations, model, request id) to your tenant log stream; retention and push to your SIEM is configurable.
[03:50] Liam O'Connor: Are the application audit logs tamper-evident / immutable? We need an immutable chain for some regs.
[03:58] Jordan Patel: We support append-only audit streams with options to forward to your immutable storage. For extra assurance we can provide signed log digests periodically. There's some implementation detail to discuss in the deep dive.
[04:13] Priya Raman: Data residency: we need keys to be regionally located (EU keys for EU data). How do you support regional keys?
[04:22] Miguel Santos: We support per-tenant key scoping and regional KMS integration. For hosted deployments we can be configured to use a regional CMK in that cloud region. For Private/Dedicated you can bring a regional HSM or use your regional cloud KMS endpoint.
[04:39] Sara Kim: On the HSM option, what's the certificate/attestation process — can we get evidence of module version and tamper status?
[04:48] Jordan Patel: Yes, for on-prem or dedicated HSMs we can coordinate attestation reports and hardware logs. For cloud HSM we provide information about the module IDs and FIPS-level, and we can arrange a customer joint review.
[05:03] Liam O'Connor: Is there any latency hit when using external KMS for every decryption? Our inference calls are latency-sensitive.
[05:10] Miguel Santos: Good point — we avoid round-tripping for each inference by caching decrypted data keys in an in-memory KV cache inside the enclave/VM for a short TTL. The master CMK is used to unwrap/rewrap keys occasionally, not on every token. So per-request latency impact is minimal.
[05:30] Priya Raman: How about key compromise scenarios — if a CMK is compromised, can you rewrap and rotate quickly and ensure forward secrecy?
[05:38] Jordan Patel: We recommend a compromise plan: rotate the CMK, perform rewrap, update access policies, and we can replay or re-encrypt data keys as needed. We also support short-lived data keys to limit exposure. We'll run through an incident playbook in the deep-dive.
[05:55] Sara Kim: Regarding encryption algorithms, do you support AES-GCM or do you use AES-CBC with HMAC?
[06:01] Miguel Santos: AES-GCM for at-rest and in-transit payloads where appropriate; we follow modern best practices and can provide algorithm lists in the security pack.
[06:12] Liam O'Connor: For SSO and RBAC, if we use SAML/SSO and SCIM, can we map roles to key access? We want separation: only security team can manage keys.
[06:22] Alyssa Chen: Yes, RBAC hooks integrate with SAML groups; key management actions can be restricted to specific roles. For customer-managed KMS, the KMS permissions are controlled in your cloud account and we only act per the granted principals.
[06:37] Priya Raman: Are there any legal hold or e-discovery considerations where keys need to be preserved?
[06:44] Jordan Patel: We can support key escrow processes for legal hold, but that typically conflicts with absolute BYOK non-escrow requirements. We'll need to understand your legal constraints if you require key preservation for holds.
[06:58] Miguel Santos: Quick note on network: for Private deployments we can do air-gapped or VPC peering. KMS calls are routed over private links where possible.
[07:07] Sara Kim: Can you show an example of IAM policy to grant Redwood access to a CMK?
[07:12] Miguel Santos: Yes, we'll include an example in the pack. It typically grants: "kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey","kms:DescribeKey" to the Redwood service principal with resource constraints.
[07:27] Priya Raman: Any support for customer-managed HSM modules with HSM attestations?
[07:33] Jordan Patel: Yes, for Dedicated and Private we support plugging in your HSM. We'll coordinate attestation and module version checks. That tends to be the enterprise flow.
[07:44] Liam O'Connor: What about retention of logs — default retention?
[07:48] Miguel Santos: Default retention is 90 days for UI-level logs and 365 days for audit exports for paid plans, but we can customize retention and export to your SIEM or long-term S3 bucket for compliance.
[07:59] Sara Kim: Are there features to redact PII in logs? We want to avoid storing model outputs with sensitive info.
[08:05] Jordan Patel: We have pipeline hooks for scrubbers and token-level redaction before logs hit storage. That's something we configure per-tenant; we'll show our redaction guide in the security pack.
[08:19] Priya Raman: Ok, on contractual terms: does BYOK + HSM require Private deployment or can it work on Hosted?
[08:27] Alyssa Chen: BYOK with cloud KMS can work in Hosted; HSM-backed (customer-managed HSM device) usually requires Dedicated or Private. CloudHSM-based FIPS modules can be used in Hosted for many cases though if you need on-prem HSM physically colocated with keys, that's Private.
[08:45] Liam O'Connor: What about key escrow for SaaS contracts — some legal teams require Redwood to hold recovery keys.
[08:52] Alyssa Chen: That's negotiable but we push for customer control; we can discuss limited escrow for specific legal requirements but that reduces the assurance of BYOK. We'll surface options in the contract addendum.
[09:05] Miguel Santos: I'll also note there are operational costs for HSM-backed configurations; we'll include TCO and pricing differences.
[09:12] Priya Raman: Great. Can you run us through a sample flow — create CMK, grant access, run inference, audit?
[09:19] Miguel Santos: Sure: 1) Customer creates CMK in AWS KMS and grants Redwood encrypt/decrypt/GenerateDataKey. 2) When a model writes data to store, Redwood generates a data key via your CMK (GenerateDataKey) — the plaintext data key is used briefly in memory then encrypted with the CMK and the ciphertext is stored. 3) For inference, Redis or KV cache holds decrypted data key in memory with TTL; we do not persist plaintext. 4) All KMS calls are visible in your CloudTrail and Redwood app logs reference the KMS request id.
[09:58] Sara Kim: Sounds good. Are there any known limitations or blockers from integration perspective?
[10:03] Miguel Santos: Sometimes customer IAM policy scoping can be too restrictive; we'll provide minimal IAM policy examples. For on-prem HSM there is network setup and attestation time.
[10:14] Priya Raman: Ok next steps we talked about: send the security pack and schedule deep dive.
[10:20] Alyssa Chen: Yep I have action items to send docs and Jordan/Miguel will run the technical session. Anything else?
[10:26] Liam O'Connor: Please include the specific algorithm list and any FIPS module ids.
[10:30] Jordan Patel: Will do.
[10:33] Alyssa Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with proposed times.
[10:36] Priya Raman: Thanks all.
[10:38] [end of recording]
